title: Mol-Metal metric JSON v1 (tolerant)
description: Schema for files under metrics/by_metric/*.json. The required fields are listed below — these fields are EXPECTED on every metric file but the validator emits WARNING (not FAIL) when any of them are missing, preserving backward compatibility with pre-v1 metric files. Optional fields such as honest_framing, gate_target, wave, and recipe/dataset are listed in `properties`. The schema is intentionally tolerant: additionalProperties is true so unknown keys are allowed (e.g. per_seed, val_history, scorer_name).

metric_id.description: Stable metric identifier (e.g. 'm1_auc', 'm2_r2', 'decode_ratio'). Lowercase + snake_case. Null allowed for legacy files.

value.description: Canonical scalar value of the metric. Null allowed for derived/composite metrics where the scalar is computed elsewhere.

source_path.description: Path on disk to the report JSON or log that produced this metric. Convention: 'molmetal/reports/<wave>/<subdir>/<file>.json' or 'metrics/by_metric/<file>.json'.

timestamp.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when the metric was last refreshed (e.g. '2026-09-30T16:48:36Z').

gate_target.description: Threshold the metric must clear for honest-framing PASS (e.g. Krasnov 0.86 gate for m1_auc).

recipe.description: Legacy recipe string (pre-v1; validator emits WARNING when missing metric_id+value+unit+source_path+timestamp but present in its place).

status.description: One status token from the project's vocabulary: MEASURED*, PROJECTED, DEFERRED, BLOCKED, SUPERSEDED, DESIGN, PARTIAL, VERIFIED, KILL, POSITIVE, NEGATIVE, TBD, ... No whitespace: a sentence here cannot be classified and makes the row non-quotable (docs/METRIC_CITABILITY_RULE.md).

status_basis.description: Why that status applies, in one sentence. Added 2026-10-20 to the 15 artifact claims that had no status at all.

no_headline_reason.description: Declares that this file has no scalar headline BY DESIGN (probe-scale result, multi-arm table). Suppresses the generic 'no scalar headline' gap in registry.py cite.

headline_key.description: Dotted JSON path to the headline number when no generic key order can find it (e.g. 'aggregate.closure_bounded_5pocket_simple_mean'). The registry records the resolved path in the row's value_basis.

headline_caveat.description: One sentence a reader needs alongside the number even when it is table-grade: a cohort alias, a superseded baseline, a single-seed warning. Printed by registry.py cite.

n_seeds.description: Number of seeds actually run. Required for a table-grade mark; n=1 stays quotable but never table-grade.

n_runs.description: Number of independent runs, when that is the right count (a deterministic pass over a fixed cohort has n_runs=1 and no seeds).

split.description: The evaluation split (e.g. '5 seeds x 5-fold CV', 'scaffold', 'not applicable (generation)'). Required for a table-grade mark.

date_utc.description: Measurement date when it is not in `timestamp`. The registry reads timestamp / date / date_utc, then any ISO date under a date-named key, and records which one it used.

supersedes.description: One path or id this file replaces (prov:wasRevisionOf). A single path-like token only; prose belongs in supersedes_note, because a relationship that cannot be resolved cannot be checked.

superseded_by.description: One path or id that replaces this file. Makes the row non-quotable regardless of `status` -- a superseded measurement is not a current claim.

supersedes_note.description: Free-form record of what was replaced and why, when the relation is not a file-to-file pointer.

definition_status.description: REDEFINED / RECONSTRUCTED / RENAMED when the metric's definition changed. Stays quotable but can never be table-grade: values on either side of the change are not comparable.
